records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup query deletes reminders with retryCount > 1, but the retry path increments retryCount from 0 by exactly 1 per failure, so a reminder that fails once is never cleaned up and fails again on the next cron run. A reminder that errors on run 1 (retryCount becomes 1) is re-selected by the upcoming-reminders query and re-attempted; the deletion branch only fires after the second failure, so the intended one-retry cap is actually a two-failure cap and every failure path executes one extra full Twilio call + DB cycle before the record is purged. Conversely, reminders with retryCount > 1 but scheduledDate in the future that were never SMS-failed via this path would also be deleted, since the OR branch matches regardless of scheduledDate.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retry cap is off-by-one relative to any natural reading: a reminder is retried at retryCount 1 and 2, and deleted when the next run sees retryCount > 1 — so the second retry attempt is scheduled once but the row is purged at the start of that same run before it can be re-attempted. Operators tuning 'retryCount' expectations (e.g., '3 retries') get 1–2 depending on run timing, and the purge deletes rows whose incremented value was written by the immediately-preceding run in the same invocation order — the exact cap boundary is untested and undocumented.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The new deleteMany OR-branch removes reminders with retryCount > 1 regardless of scheduledDate, so a reminder whose scheduledDate is still in the future gets hard-deleted once it accumulates two failures, destroying the scheduled reminder row entirely. A transient Twilio failure twice in a row causes the reminder row to be silently deleted even though its scheduledDate has not yet passed; the attendee never receives the reminder and no record of the missed reminder exists for auditing or manual re-send.
records.rationale: The diff changes `deleteMany` to `where: { OR: [ { method: SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: now } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] }`, which will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1` regardless of `scheduledDate` (and even regardless of `method`). Since later in the same handler the code increments `retryCount` on failures (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` in both the `else` branch and `catch`), a reminder that fails twice can be hard-deleted on the next run even if its `scheduledDate` is still in the future, matching the finding’s data-loss behavior.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Retry-give-up is implemented by silently deleting the reminder on the next scheduler pass (retryCount > 1) with no logging, notification, or state marking on the abandonment path, and the retry counter is only surfaced via console.log on the error path. Operators get no signal when reminders are abandoned after retries exhaust — a reminder that fails twice disappears from the database entirely, making debugging missed SMS reminders impossible because the evidence row is deleted.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The retryCount>1 delete clause has no method filter, so it deletes WorkflowReminder rows of every method (email, SMS, etc.), not just SMS reminders. WorkflowReminder is a shared table across reminder methods; the OR branch { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } matches any row with retryCount > 1. Today only this SMS path increments retryCount, but the schema change makes retryCount a general column on WorkflowReminder, so any future (or parallel) method that uses it — e.g. an email retry implementation touching the same model — has its reminders silently hard-deleted by the SMS cron. The original code carefully scoped deletion to method: WorkflowMethods.SMS; the new branch drops that invariant.

This breaks the previous invariant (and even the nearby comment) that deletion is scoped to SMS reminders only, and becomes more problematic because `retryCount` is added as a general column on `WorkflowReminder` in the schema/migration.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch block increments retryCount even when the error is thrown after Twilio has already accepted and scheduled the SMS, causing duplicate SMS sends on retry. The try block spans the Twilio schedule call and the subsequent reminder bookkeeping. If the Twilio call succeeds but any later statement in the try (e.g. the create/update of the reminder record with referenceId) throws, the catch increments retryCount, the reminder is never marked as scheduled (no referenceId row tying it to the sid), and the next cron run re-invokes Twilio — the attendee gets the same reminder SMS twice or three times. The retry counter conflates 'send failed' with 'bookkeeping after send failed'.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retryCount>1 deletion is unbounded by scheduledDate, deleting rows from any time period including the deep past, on every cron tick. Unlike the scheduledDate branch, the retryCount branch scans/deletes across all history each run. With no upper bound it also deletes old failed rows that the scheduledDate branch would have caught anyway, meaning two deletion predicates in the same deleteMany overlap semantically and the reason a given row vanished (past-date vs retry-cap) is unauditable. Operationally: an admin investigating why a reminder disappeared cannot tell which clause removed it.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The new deleteMany OR-branch deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of scheduledDate, so the endpoint now permanently drops reminders after two failed attempts instead of just clearing past-date SMS reminders. A reminder that fails twice (e.g., a transient Twilio outage or an invalid phone number) is deleted from the database with scheduledDate still in the future, so the attendee never receives the reminder and there is no record that it was ever attempted — the stated intent of 'retry count tracking' silently became 'delete after 2 tries', a data-loss behavior change with no human-accepted spec for it.

That means this handler will hard-delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` row (including non-SMS methods) once `retryCount > 1`, and it can do so even if the reminder is not past due. records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch-block prisma.workflowReminder.update can itself throw (P2025 record-not-found) with no surrounding try, turning a handled Twilio failure into an unhandled exception that aborts the remaining loop iterations and returns a 500. If the reminder row is deleted between the initial fetch and the catch (e.g., a concurrent invocation's deleteMany with retryCount > 1, or a booking cancellation deleting reminders), the update inside catch throws, the for-loop over unscheduledReminders exits early, all subsequent reminders in this batch are never scheduled, and the caller gets a 500 instead of the partial-success shape the endpoint otherwise returns.

If the reminder row is deleted between the initial `findMany` and this update (plausible given the new `deleteMany` OR clause that deletes any reminder with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`), Prisma can throw (e.g., P2025 record not found), which would escape the catch and abort the loop/handler.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] retryCount increment is read-then-write (reminder.retryCount + 1 from the earlier querySnapshot result), not an atomic { increment: 1 }, so overlapping invocations lose increments. Two concurrent handler invocations (overlapping cron runs or a retried request) both read retryCount=0 and both write 1, so the deletion-based retry cap under-counts and failed reminders persist and retry far beyond the intended 2 attempts. Using data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } removes the race.

Since `reminder.retryCount` comes from an earlier `findMany` snapshot, overlapping handler executions can both read the same value and both write the same incremented value, losing one increment.
